answer: Sleep supports memory, immune function, and emotional wellbeing. Most adults need 7–9 hours of sleep per night.

knowledge_sources.content:
### Optimal Bedtime

For most adults, the ideal sleep window is 10:00–11:30 PM, when melatonin secretion peaks naturally. Going to bed consistently each night anchors the circadian clock.

### Sleep Cycle Maths

One sleep cycle is 90 minutes. To wake at 6:30 AM refreshed, go to sleep at 9:00 PM, 10:30 PM, or midnight to complete a whole number of cycles.

### Recommended Duration

Adults aged 18–60 need at least 7 hours nightly; adults 61–64 should target 7–9 hours. Regularly sleeping fewer than 7 hours is associated with health risks.

### Chronotypes

Early chronotypes prefer to sleep and wake earlier; night owls prefer later schedules. Chronotype is partly genetic and tends to shift later during the teenage years.

### Evening Routine

Dimming lights 1–2 hours before bed and avoiding screens after 9 PM reduces sleep onset time. A cool bedroom of 16–19 °C also improves sleep quality.
